contexts.text: The brightness of fire round about from the loins downward, as the bow in the cloud () = the Celestial Spiritual, (the brightness. and rainbow = wisdom and intelligence. AC 3021:6.)
The resplendence induces the appearance of a garment.
Illumination and power is signified by brightness, and light ().
The splendour of the colours there. Their splendour is from the truth which is of intelligence...
Those who have loved to live splendidly...
If love to the Lord and charity towards the neighbour had formed their interiors, there is a derivative resplendence in their faces.

Spirits appear in garments devoid of resplendence; but Angels in garments which have resplendence, and which are as if formed from resplendence; for the resplendence itself around them appears as a garment... The resplendence in their garments is from the good of love and of charity; for this good by its shining through confers resplendence.

Truth from the Divine is represented by garments of such bright whiteness and resplendence; because the brightness and resplendence of Heaven are from the light which is from the Lord, which is Divine truth. Illustrated.
Those appear in bright resplendent garments who are in truths of faith which are from good; for the good shines through the truth: whence is the resplendence.
To wait for brightnesses () = the good of truth; for the resplendence of light is from good. AE 526:11.
No longer to have light from faith and love is to withdraw their shining ().
The Angels appear... in beauty and resplendence according to the quality of the good from truths.
To shine as the stars () = to be in the intelligence of truth and the wisdom of good, and thence in eternal happiness.
That at the Lord's presence the internal sense appears, such as it is in Heaven, in its glory, is signified by, at the brightness before Him His clouds passed away (). AE 594:6.
Divine truth in Heaven itself resplendent from the good of love. Signified, Explained.

That the plate = illustration, was from its resplendence; for it shone from the gold upon Aaron's forehead; and all resplendence = illustration (or enlightenment) such as there is in the Heavens from the Lord as a Sun.

Fatuous lumen shines before their eyes from things confirmatory and persuasive: whether it is false, or true, it shines. But this resplendence becomes mere thick darkness when light from Heaven inflows.
These appear clothed in white resplendent garments.
The resplendence is from the Divine good.
The brightness of her glory () = the love of truth from the Lord. ( = Divine truth from which is doctrine. AE 365:39.)
See Garment. HH 181.
Those in this love are in heavenly intelligence, and in Heaven shine as with the brightness of the expanse (). HH 356:3. HH 518, Explained.
Falsities, when confirmed, may shine; but not in the light of Heaven.
Man may dwell and live splendidly according to his condition...
All resplendent as with gold, etc.
It is Divine truth which shines in Heaven... and use turns the rays of this light into various resplendences.
He lived splendidly every day () = because they had and read the Word.
After His advent the Sun appeared in greater resplendence.
Divine fire and Divine resplendence in the Sun; and from the Sun spiritual heat and light.
The surface of the love of self makes a certain resplendence of light...

Fat and splendid things () = celestial and spiritual affections of good and truth... Affections of truth are called splendid, because they come forth from the light of Heaven, and its resplendence in minds...
Fine linen clean and bright () = brilliant from good, and pure from truth. (It is called bright from spiritual good. AE 1222.)
The brightness round about () = the derivative Divine wisdom.
Bright as crystal () = these truths translucent from the spiritual sense, which is in the light of Heaven.
The bright and morning Star () = that He was the light...
All things in that Society are splendid and magnificent; splendid from the gold and precious stones... And all good uses shine in the Heavens.
In the maidens, there is only the lustre; but in the wives, the resplendence of beauty.
The light of conjugial love filled the house with resplendence.
From the resplendence of fire proceeds light. So in love... there is something inmostly affecting the understanding to which the resplendence of fire I corresponds. TCR 41.
They who have performed uses from love towards the neighbour... are in splendour and I honour there.
To make the darkness shine () = to dissipate the falsities of ignorance with the light of truth.
The brightness of Jehovah, and the light () = the Divine truth.
The resplendence of the light or of the Divine truth proceeding from Him is from the Divine love.
The brightness of thy rising () = Divine truth from Divine good whence is intelligence.
The enlightenment of the man of the Church by the reception and after the reception of Divine truth from the Lord's Divine good, is signified by the clear shining after rain ().

Clothed in linen clean and bright () = by Divine truth, or the Word from the spiritual sense... It is called bright from the light in Heaven; which light is resplendence; for from it all things there shine. AE 951. AE 1159.
